 ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. -- When it comes to headlines about the Brewers' starting pitchers, Jacob Misiorowski understandably gets the lion's share of attention. But not to be lost in the shuffle is Robert Gasser.
 The lefty from California, who struck out 103 batters during the regular season, will get the start in Game 3 of the World Series as his team hopes to take a commanding 3-0 lead.
 Gasser was exactly what his team needed him to be during his first two outings this postseason. He allowed just 1 run over 4 innings in the NLDS against the Padres and followed that up with a scoreless 5-inning outing in the NLCS against the Dodgers.
 News 
 Milwaukee still loves him, but Freddy Peralta will try beating the Brewers in World Series Game 3 
 By STEVE MEGARGEE - AP Sports Writer 
 Both of those starts came on the road, showing Gasser can perform well in front of a hostile crowd in the postseason. On both occasions, he left his manager Pat Murphy in a good position to hand things over to the bullpen, which has been dominant all postseason.
 That, truthfully, is all Milwaukee needs from its starting rotation. A solid 5-inning start from Gasser will allow the three-headed monster of Abner Uribe, Aaron Ashby and Trevor Megill to reliably take the game the rest of the way.
 But Gasser will need run support, and to do that Milwaukee's batters will need to vanquish an old friend.
 Freddy Peralta's journey to the World Series is a fascinating one. The Brewers traded him to the Mets before the start of the 2026 campaign to avoid paying him out a massive new contract. He had been an ace for the Brewers over the course of 8 seasons, especially after the departure of Corbin Burnes, and posted a career-best 2.70 ERA in 2025.
 But Peralta's time in New York was nothing short of nightmarish. In 22 starts he allowed 63 earned runs, including 17 home runs. He was booed by the home fans, and it ultimately became clear he wasn't the right fit for the Mets.
 In August, the Mets shipped Peralta to the Tampa Bay Rays. The move seemed to revitalize him. In 10 starts, he posted a 3.25 ERA including a 0.96 ERA in September. He notched 43 strikeouts across those 10 starts and allowed 41 hits.
 In the postseason, "Fastball Freddy" has looked like vintage form. He allowed 1 run over 4.2 innings against the Yankees then shut the Guardians down in Game 2 of the ALCS with 6 strikeouts. He served as a relief pitcher when his team needed him in Game 4, then started Game 6 two nights later and helped his team clinch the series with a strong 5.1-inning outing.
 Now, the Rays will need that vintage Freddy again. Down 2-0, Tampa will need all they can get to defend their home turf and get back into the series.
 Meanwhile, the Brewers will hope a strong start from "Bobby Diesel" and familiarity with Peralta's game can get them one step closer to World Series glory.
 Game 3 starts at 7 p.m. on Monday, and News 3 Now will have coverage live from Florida throughout the day leading up to first pitch.
